what_it_does: This paper describes a tiny AI accelerator (MAE) that runs autoencoder models—image compression networks used in generative AI—on edge devices like phones and robots. The core problem is that these devices have very little fast on-chip memory, forcing the chip to constantly fetch data from slower external memory, which burns up to 80% of the energy budget. The approach uses a specialized scheduling strategy called 'line-based depth-first fusion' to organize how data flows through the chip, keeping more data locally available and reusing it efficiently. The chip integrates 576 multiply-accumulate units (the tiny math engines that power neural nets) into an area smaller than a grain of sand (0.168 mm² in 3nm process), making it practical for real devices.
